title: Illinois officials investigate attempted cyberattack on Algonquin Dam
date_note: Gizmodo (published 21 Nov) says the operator detected the Nov. 16 incident; the disclosure was reported around 20 to 21 Nov.
geo_basis: Algonquin Dam on the Fox River, Illinois, as named by Gizmodo; town centre
summary: Gizmodo reports that the Illinois Department of Natural Resources said Algonquin Dam on the Fox River "was subject to a cyberattack earlier this week"; the dam operator detected the Nov. 16 incident. The Chicago Tribune and ABC 7 described it as an attempted cyberattack. IDNR said it took immediate action to keep the dam secure and fully operational; an IDNR spokesperson had not returned Gizmodo's request for more information.
plain: Illinois officials say Algonquin Dam was subject to a cyberattack. Two news outlets call it an attempt. IDNR says it acted to keep the dam secure and fully operational.
exec: A US dam operator reports a cyberattack; IDNR says the dam stayed secure and fully operational.
action: No action needed; for awareness. Operators of dams and water systems can watch for IDNR and CISA updates.
impact: IDNR says it took immediate action to keep the dam secure and fully operational.

validation.note: Gizmodo read; it relays the IDNR statement and the Chicago Tribune and ABC 7 reports. The Chicago Tribune page could not be loaded and the IDNR release was not read.

review.note: Gizmodo read: removed unsupported 'no affected systems were reported' (summary, impact); 'attempted' now attributed to Chicago Tribune and ABC 7; added Nov. 16 detection; spokesperson wording matched; plain and exec aligned. Stays single_source; Tribune page and IDNR release not read.
